extracted.intended_audience: users of the Brookings Deregulatory Tracker (researchers, journalists, policy analysts, and general public interested in tracking deregulatory actions)
extracted.subtask_description: Defines what deregulatory actions the Brookings Deregulatory Tracker includes and excludes, how entries are discovered, presented, filtered, sorted, and updated, and how to interpret timelines and ‘noteworthy’ labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of actions included
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reg Tracker monitors a curated selection of delayed, repealed, and new rules, notable guidance and policy revocations, and important court battles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes actions across many policy areas (education, finance, environment, transportation, etc.). Also includes guidance revocations and executive actions that have immediate, unmistakably 'deregulatory' impact (example: Executive Order 13783 withdrawing social cost of carbon technical documents). Includes rules rescinded through the Congressional Review Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking process tracked (timeline/status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each regulation in the Reg Tracker has a timeline that monitors that entry’s status in the process (e.g., 'proposed', 'final', 'effective').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All proposed and final rules are required to be published in the Federal Register; hover over the question mark on an entry to view a key explaining timeline statuses. The tracker focuses on the stages of rulemaking and reflects changes to an entry’s procedural status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of non-notice-and-comment actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reg Tracker includes some deregulatory actions that don’t proceed through notice and comment, such as guidance revocations and executive actions with immediate deregulator effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions that do not proceed through notice and comment will often have a descriptive box in place of the usual timeline to reflect the different procedural nature of the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) rescissions included
rubrics_metrics.description: The tracker includes rules that were rescinded through use of the Congressional Review Act (CRA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains CRA procedure: all rules must be reported to Congress; upon receipt Congress has 60 legislative working days to introduce a joint resolution of disapproval; historically rare but used frequently by the Trump administration. Notes that CRA resolutions require presidential signature to become law, so the president’s view largely determines reversal under CRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: How entries are chosen (source scanning)
rubrics_metrics.description: A team of Brookings staff scans every issue of the Federal Register for items that are deregulatory in nature, and also scans major and specialty news sources and major court proceedings (notably the D.C. Circuit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included items are those that are deregulatory in nature (e.g., effective date delays of prior rules, final rule withdrawals, proposals to withdraw or rework old regulations). The team excludes withdrawals of proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion criteria — scope limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reg Tracker is not intended to be comprehensive and does not include every single deregulatory action made by the administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not provide cost estimates of new or proposed rules and excludes actions like selective enforcement and budget reprogramming even though they can be deregulatory. Items that are arcane, routine, or uncontroversial are usually excluded. Withdrawals of proposed rules are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noteworthiness designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain entries are marked as 'Noteworthy' for users who want to focus on a few important deregulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Noteworthy' regulations are those that have a particularly significant impact and are at the forefront of President Trump's deregulatory agenda; these can be isolated via a 'Noteworthy only' filter in the selection bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update frequency and last-updated metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reg Tracker is updated approximately every week to reflect new deregulatory actions or updates to existing actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every entry is updated weekly—only those with new actions. Each entry shows a 'last updated' date next to its heading indicating when that particular entry was last changed by staff (entries may have been reviewed later without a change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sorting rules for entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are sorted by default by the 'last updated' date, but users can change sorting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New entries (changed within the last 14 days) appear at the top and are indicated by a yellow 'New' tag. Entries can also be sorted by name, category, agency, or status by clicking respective headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtering capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Users may filter entries based on category, status, agency, and noteworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: view only entries in a particular category (environmental, education, etc.), with a certain status (in rulemaking, effective, etc.), or by the rule’s 'noteworthiness.' Filters are available in the selection bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curatorial emphasis — newsworthiness and alignment with agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: The tracker favors actions that are newsworthy or consistent with the administration's deregulatory agenda when selecting entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team includes items that are economically or politically significant, controversial, or otherwise newsworthy rather than attempting exhaustive coverage of all deregulatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation differences for non-rule actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation format differs depending on the procedural type of action; non-rule actions may not use the timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For items that do not proceed through notice and comment (e.g., guidance revocations, executive actions), the tracker will often use a descriptive box instead of the timeline to present the action and its effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded content types explicitly noted
rubrics_metrics.description: The tracker explicitly notes types of deregulatory conduct it does not include or quantify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically states it does not include cost estimates and omits actions such as selective enforcement and budget reprogramming, clarifying the tool’s limitations for users seeking comprehensive deregulatory measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of policy areas covered
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reg Tracker covers a wide range of policy areas, but selection is curated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy areas explicitly mentioned include education, finance, environment, and transportation; inclusion depends on significance/newsworthiness rather than exhaustive coverage of all areas.
